expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "No — 'table isn't empty' wouldn't have caught this"

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "'COALESCE(x, 0)' on a join result is doing the same thing as `except: pass` — it converts a loud failure (nulls propagating, dashboard breaking visibly) into a quiet, plausible-looking wrong number"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation: warehouse total vs. source-system total...Only 'does the sum match the source' catches a join silently dropping data"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Asks "does this test run *before* the table is published?" but does not recommend it should

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: No data contract or schema check mentioned

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Null-rate assertion on the join key" and "a volume check with the floor set at zero"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses the gap ("A three-week miss usually means...") but does not treat it as needing its own fix

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: "a row-count check, a null check, a schema check — all of those can pass on a perfectly well-formed, wrong number. Only 'does the sum match the source' catches a join silently dropping data"
